The only litre figure it gives is a warning threshold: the low-urea indication appears below Urea 5.4 liter, and when the "Low Urea" message shows with the SCR warning lamp the urea tank needs to be refilled (p.663). It also notes refilling is needed approximately every 5,600 km, with consumption depending on road profile, driving pattern and environmental conditions (p.666), and that only ISO 22241- or DIN 70070-specified urea solution may be used (p.668).

Practical takeaway: buy a 10 L canister and fill to the tank mark; don't force extra in, since the handbook warns an over-filled tank can expand when frozen and seriously damage the tank or urea system (p.666).

**DPF = Diesel Particulate Filter.**

The Hyundai Tucson 2021–2023 owner handbook spells it out when describing the warning lamp: if the accumulated soot is out of the detection range, the soot oxidization process does not occur, and the Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF) lamp illuminates (p.730).

What it does, per the same handbook (p.730): it burns off (or oxidizes) the accumulated soot in accordance with driving situations, unlike a disposable air filter — the accumulated soot is automatically purged out by the engine control system and by the high exhaust-gas temperature at normal/high driving speeds. When the vehicle is continually driven at repeated short distances or at low speed for a long time, the accumulated soot may not be automatically removed because of low exhaust gas temperature (p.730). It also warns that the lamp stops illuminating when the driving speed exceeds 37 mph (60 km/h), or when the engine rpm is between 1,250 and 2,500 with the gear in the 2nd position or above for approximately 25 minutes (p.730) — note that regeneration figure is specific to that Tucson, not a universal value.

Fuel caution (Tucson 2015–2020, p.9): fuel with high sulfur (more than 50 ppm sulfur) and unspecified additives can cause the DPF system to be damaged and white smoke can be emitted.

Source: Hyundai Tucson 2021–2023 owner handbook p.730 and Hyundai Tucson 2015–2020 owner handbook p.9 — both owner handbooks, not workshop manuals. No car is pinned, so if you want the regeneration conditions and DPF lamp behaviour for your own car, tell me the make, model, year and engine.
